title: Bleaching values were scarce before 2003 in the Reef Check part of BCO-DMO 773466 version 2
abstract: We audited outcome availability in 14,430 distinct Reef Check surveys from 1997 to 2019 in BCO-DMO dataset 773466 version 2. Only 73 of 2,202 early surveys had a bleaching percentage, or 3.32%. Reporting rose to 87.97% in 2003-2009 and 94.40% in 2010-2019. At 206 sites sampled in both 1998-2002 and 2003-2007, the site mean reporting rate rose by 67.91 percentage points. The country bootstrap interval was 54.25 to 82.55 points. Each ocean group had a positive change. Site turnover alone cannot explain this pattern. The sign of a simple late-minus-early bleaching mean is not identified when missing outcomes can range from 0 to 100%. The archive does not show whether the gap arose in collection, reporting, or field mapping. This result applies to the named flat field, not all Reef Check data. The package gives a coverage map, survey records, code, bounds, source hashes, and an independent count check.

display.caption: Reported outcome rates by ocean and year, and worst-case bounds for mean bleaching among archived surveys.
